notes.purpose: jaxfne/fields is the source→field / laminar-projection subpackage: it turns simulated spike/Vm sources into proxy field readouts (LFP/CSD/EEG/MEG/EMM) and spectrolaminar analysis, plus one experimental PDE solver. It's organized as 4 concern-split files (not one-file-per-concern-per-signal-type but a 4-way split by role): `proxy.py` (the big math engine: source projection, spectrolaminar PSD/bandpower/readout/objective, cable filters, csd_tensor — 1309 lines, by far the largest file), `probes.py` (thin `ProbeReadout`-returning wrappers per modality: spk/vm/source/lfp/csd/eeg/meg/emm probes + eeg/meg/emm proxy_transform helpers, 363 lines), `diagnostics.py` (validation/reporting helpers factored out of proxy.py to "keep mathematical projection code clean" per its own module docstring, 166 lines), and `solvers.py` (an independent, explicitly "experimental" 1D Poisson PDE solver bridged to Model.neuron_table()/Signals.sources, 253 lines, most recently touched d387866). `__init__.py` (103 lines) is a pure re-export aggregator gathering all four files' public names into the subpackage surface, which `jaxfne/core.py` line 37 re-imports 3 of (FieldOutput, probe_laminar_modes, project_laminar_sources) into the top-level jtfne namespace.

diagnostics.py's _dtype_name, _finite_bool, _test_kernel_row_normalization are internal-only underscore helpers, but proxy.py deliberately re-imports them (proxy.py lines 24-29) with an explicit comment: 'Canonical source for these field diagnostics/validation helpers is diagnostics.py. They are imported (not redefined) here so that fields.proxy.<name> continues to resolve' -- this is a documented dedup pattern, not accidental duplication.

core.py line 37 imports only 3 of the 39 fields exports into the top-level namespace (FieldOutput, probe_laminar_modes, project_laminar_sources); core.py line 201 references compute_fields separately (likely from elsewhere, not fields/__init__ -- not verified further).

proxy.py's own module docstring (lines 1-8) states: 'This module implements structural simulation proxy calculations under linear_solver. Physical amplitude claims remain uncalibrated (amplitude_claim_allowed=False).' -- an explicit truth-gate declaration at the file level.

solvers.py is explicitly labeled experimental (module docstring line 1: 'Experimental PDE field solvers for jaxfne') and is the newest/most actively touched file (git log shows 3 recent commits: d387866 bridging it to Model.neuron_table()/Signals.sources, ef17134 verifying flux conservation + documenting an N~150-200 convergence ceiling, b62d560 extending it to layered conductivity).
contracts: core.py re-exports fields/ as one of its aggregator sources (AGENTS.md line 105: 'core.py re-exports → _config.py, _model.py, _signals.py, _construct.py, _runtime_config.py, emitters.py, fields/.') -- verified by core.py:37 actually importing from .fields.

Modular-grammar rule: plotting confined to jaxfne/vis/* only (AGENTS.md line 106: 'Plotting: jaxfne/vis/* only (modular-grammar rule 2)') -- fields/ itself contains no plotting code (grep of the 4 files shows no matplotlib/plotly imports), consistent with this rule; it produces numeric proxy arrays for vis/ to plot, not figures itself.

Amplitude-claim truth gate: proxy.py declares amplitude_claim_allowed=False and repeatedly uses 'uncalibrated'/'proxy' language (29 hits across fields/*.py for amplitude_claim_allowed/physical_amplitude_calibrated/uncalibrated) -- callers must not upgrade these proxy outputs to 'physical'/'calibrated' claims without a real calibration step elsewhere.

Re-export identity contract: diagnostics.py is the canonical source for _dtype_name/_finite_bool/_test_kernel_row_normalization; proxy.py must import (not redefine) them -- enforced by tests/test_fields_helper_dedup_v0330.py::test_proxy_names_are_identical_objects per FRICTIONS_STACK.md row F-030.

Docs contract: proxy.py's docstring (line 3) points to docs/api/fields.md ('update that page when this module's public API changes') -- not verified whether that doc file exists/is current, but it's a stated obligation on any public-API edit to proxy.py.
landmines: FRICTIONS_STACK.md row F-030 (line 38) directly implicates this subpackage: a `ruff check --fix` pass previously gutted core.py/_construct.py of re-export blocks (breaking `import jaxfne` outright) AND separately, on a corrected second pass, silently deleted _dtype_name/_test_kernel_row_normalization from fields/proxy.py's re-export block from diagnostics.py -- caught only by the full test suite (tests/test_fields_helper_dedup_v0330.py::test_proxy_names_are_identical_objects), not by inspection, because proxy.py's F401 count (4) was below the heuristic threshold used to flag re-export files. Lesson stated in that row: low F401 count is not a safe proxy for 'not a re-export' when lint-auto-fixing this subpackage.

solvers.py's own docstring documents a real numerical limitation: 'a real N~150-200 convergence ceiling' for experimental_poisson_1d (per commit ef17134's message) -- this is stated as a known constraint, not a bug, but any caller pushing N higher should expect degraded convergence per that documented ceiling.

A stray jaxfne/fields/.DS_Store (6148 bytes) sits in the subpackage directory -- not a landmine in the functional sense but is repo-root-freeze noise the doctrine's 'keep repo roots thin' rule would flag if noticed during a commit.
